title: Walter Beatty and his tap dance walk
summary: Green describes Walter Beatty, a heavy, light-footed comedian who introduced the tap dance walk with character walks, and partnered Foster.

story.theme_name: Pianists: who played, who influenced whom
story.community_name: Who played piano: the pianists musicians remembered

blocks.x: Well, what other members of the Hoofer's Club? You had mentioned Tip, Tap and Toe. And I remember you recalling a --
Oh, yeah. Well, there was Walter Beatty.

He was famous for tap dancing, because he introduced the tap dance walk, see. Otherwise -- if you can walk you can dance, and tap dancing is like walking. So he would demonstrate this, how to walk tap dancing. He's just
put some music to the walking and you hear yourself, hear your feet, and that's tap dancing.
Easier said than done, I'm sure.
Well, did he add a little routine to that? Did he do different types of walk? This is how you walk when you're happy, this is how you walk when you're sad?
What was the nature of his routine?
Yes, that was him. That's his work. That's exactly the way.
Yes. He did do -- how he would walk if he couldn't see his best girl, and how he would walk when he finally did see her. Then how he'd walk after he had done seen her, you see.
What other kinds of things would he do in his routine?

Well, he had a way of being light on his feet, you see, because he looked to be the size of about, I'd say a little over 300 pounds. And he was very tall, see. And he had a what do you call it -- such shiny cheeks, see. He was very versatile, see. He done blackface comedian. He did the Foster and Beatty. That was a duo. In other words, he acquired a partner. He took Jonah's place. Used to be Jonah
and Foster. But he was famous before then, you see. But he was one of the Hoofer's Club's members, you see.
Were they known mostly for their dancing, or was their act a mixture of tricks, walks, jokes, things like that? Were they really a top dancing --

Yeah. They were clever, see. Especially Walter Beatty. He was about one of the cleverest that they ever had at the Hoofer's Club. As I say, he was versatile. He had a great singing voice. He worked in and out of blackface. He wore the high hat and tails. But he was greatly known for his tap dancing. His tap dancing was loved mostly. But he was a great comedian, also.
